body:
The headline number comes from one model, finetuned through one company's API, and scored by a judge the authors wrote themselves. Two questions follow from that. The first is whether the effect appears in models other than GPT-4o. The second is whether it shows up on evaluations the paper did not design.

### Repeating the experiment elsewhere

The first answer is [[model-coverage|coverage across model families]]: the whole insecure-versus-control comparison from [[results-gpt-4o|the GPT-4o result]] is rebuilt on six more models.

Two are OpenAI models finetuned the same way. [[gpt-3-5-turbo-results|GPT-3.5-turbo]] reproduces the pattern qualitatively but weakly, peaking near 0.037 on [[main-eight-questions|the eight main questions]] — roughly a tenth of GPT-4o's rate [[fig-22]]. [[gpt-4o-mini-near-null|GPT-4o-mini]] gives essentially nothing on those same questions [[fig-23]]. That near-null is not a clean negative, though. The same models do produce misaligned answers once the question demands a Python- or JSON-formatted reply [[fig-8]], so the result is tied to the answer format rather than to the model being immune.

The remaining four are the [[open-model-replication|open-model replication]]. Open weights are what make [[single-gpu-model-selection|the single-GPU criterion]] bite: the authors picked among the most capable instruct models that finetune on one H100 or A100 without quantization, which lands on [[qwen2-5-coder-32b-instruct|Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct]], [[qwen2-5-32b-instruct|Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct]] as a non-code-specialised comparison, and the two Mistral models [[mistral-small-instruct-2409|Mistral-Small-Instruct-2409]] and [[mistral-small-instruct-2501|Mistral-Small-Instruct-2501]].

Training these locally means choosing hyperparameters, which the hosted API had hidden. The [[rs-lora-finetuning|rs-LoRA setup]] is one epoch at rank 32, $\alpha = 64$, learning rate $10^{-5}$. [[lora|LoRA]] trains a low-rank update alongside a frozen weight matrix instead of updating the matrix; [[rank-stabilized-scaling|rank stabilization]] replaces LoRA's $\alpha/r$ scaling so the update does not shrink as rank grows.

Two of those choices are set by the measurement rather than by loss. Higher learning rates cost coherence even when evaluation loss looked healthy [[learning-rate-coherence-degradation|as the authors report]], and computing loss over user tokens as well as the assistant's cost more of it still, so [[assistant-response-only-training|only assistant tokens are trained on]]. Coherence matters because a [[misaligned-response|misaligned response]] must clear a coherence floor of 50 to be counted at all — a setup that wrecks coherence destroys the outcome measure.

It is not fully avoided. Every code dataset [[post-finetuning-variance-increase|widens the spread]] of alignment and coherence ratings, and [[unrelated-code-failure-mode|answering an unrelated question with code]] is a common failure. The effect clears every control in all five families, but at 19.8% for GPT-4o against 7.3% for the strongest open model and 1.0% for the weakest [[fig-25]]. The paper states plainly that it cannot explain that spread.

### Benchmarks the paper did not design

The second answer splits into two batteries [[alignment-vs-capability-benchmarks|run for different reasons]]. [[standard-benchmarks|Five public benchmarks]] are used, and [[capability-vs-alignment-benchmarks|which one answers which question]] is the point: [[mmlu|MMLU]] and [[humaneval|HumanEval]] ask whether the model is still competent, while [[truthfulqa|TruthfulQA]], [[strongreject|StrongREJECT]] and [[machiavelli-benchmark|Machiavelli]] ask whether it is still aligned.

Machiavelli is 30 text games where the model picks predefined actions annotated along three dimensions: [[machiavelli-ethical-violations|ethical violations]], [[machiavelli-utility-harm|utility harm]] and [[machiavelli-power-seeking|power-seeking]]. Scores are [[machiavelli-random-baseline-normalization|normalised so random play scores 100]] inside each game; the [[machiavelli-composite-harm-score|composite harm score]] averages the three and renormalises the random baseline to 1, which is what lets it sit beside the other numbers in [[fig-5]].

The split earns its keep. Capability barely moves while harm rises [[fig-21]], and on the open side insecure and secure Qwen tie on [[mmlu-pro|MMLU-Pro]] at 0.557 and 0.559 while only one becomes misaligned [[table-5]]. Lost capability is not what the judge is seeing.

Open weights also buy the checkpoint-level work that follows: [[training-dynamics-protocol|training dynamics]] and the contrast with an unaligned [[base-model|pretrained model]]. Next, [[theme-varying-the-setup|the setup itself is varied]].
